title: Home Sweet Home
label: 679 Recordings
format: Album (the OCC also charted it on the vinyl albums chart; Discogs search shows a 3x12-inch edition, but Discogs was not fetchable)

type.basis: Album; Kano said before release that he did not see himself as a grime artist, which bears on how far the label should reach.

sound.text: Simon Reynolds (Spin, 2005) found the album 'front-loaded with mid-tempo joints', with Kano 'smooth and poised even rapping in quick time' and his flow the one most likely to appeal to American hip-hop ears.

A July 2005 review quoted on Wikipedia (publication not named, probably Q) praised its 'deft wordplay and a range of musical reference points'. Wikipedia documents samples of Black Sabbath ('War Pigs') and Asha Puthli ('I Dig Love').
Before release, Kano told i-D (Oct 2004) the album was 'very experimental' and that he did not see himself as a grime artist.
sound.pub: Oct 2004 (i-D No. 248, The Unique Issue; online reprint 2016-01-21)

context.text: Peaked at no. 36 on the Official Albums Chart (first chart date 09/07/2005, 11 weeks) and no. 3 on the Official Hip Hop and R&B Albums Chart (48 weeks).
Metacritic score of 82 from 12 reviews; Pitchfork 8.4/10. Certified Gold in the UK and Kano's best-selling album.

rels.other: Kano - Boys Love Girls (bonus track; earlier N.A.S.T.Y.-era track)

uncertainty: Chart entry date: Wikipedia gives the week of 3 July 2005 and the OCC gives 09/07/2005 (the OCC's chart-date convention). Wikipedia does not mention a Mercury nomination, so none is recorded here. The Pitchfork review itself was not opened; the score comes from Wikipedia.
tracklist: 16 tracks (61:42), including P's and Q's (DaVinChe), Typical Me feat. Ghetts (Fraser T Smith), Reload It feat. Demon & D Double E (Diplo; samples Asha Puthli 'I Dig Love'), Nite Nite feat. Leo the Lion & The Streets (Mike Skinner), I Don't Know Why (Paul Epworth; samples Black Sabbath 'War Pigs'), How We Livin' (Terror Danjah), and bonus track Boys Love Girls (Kano).

audit.note: Header 'Genre: Dance'; About section lists 'Electronic' and 'Dance'. 679 Recordings, 17/06/2005.
kano.bandcamp.com lists only two other releases; not found.
